we observe the formation of long-lived excitonic ground-states in the indirect regime of the Gamma -X transition in GaAs/ AlAs coupled quantum well heterostructures.

We report on the observation of a huge increase of exciton lifetimes in electric-field-tunable coupled quantum well structures, caused by the formation of real- (GaAs) and k-space (AlAs) indirect excitons.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the exciton dynamics in the regime of indirect excitons.
the formation of excitonic ground states and their possible condensation.
the optical properties of coupled quantum wells in the purely indirect exciton regime.

the present experiments are not yet able to provide a clear evidence for the formation of a k-space exciton Bose condensate, but the present data are in very good qualitative agreement with the theory of indirect exciton condensation.
we have found no evidence for k-space condensation in our samples.
the exciton condensate is not formed, at least in the regime of our experiments.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found a new way to create and study long-lived excitonic states in semiconductor quantum structures.
we were able to show that the indirect exciton is a very interesting and useful system for future studies of many-body physics.
the indirect exciton state is a very promising candidate to search for the excitonic Bose condensation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the indirect exciton is a very promising system for the investigation of quantum phase transitions.
indirect excitons are a promising candidate for the realization of excitonic Bose-Einstein condensation in k-space.
the indirect regime of coupled quantum wells offers a unique opportunity for the study of long-lived excitonic ground-state phenomena.
